newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria wants Anglophone regional bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria wants Anglophone regional bourse.

text.p: Nigeria is discussing with Anglophone West African countries the possibility of starting a regional stock exchange, an official of the Nigerian bourse said on Friday.
"The exchange will facilitate cross-border trading among the members," Ndi Okereke-Onyuike, a senior official of the Nigerian Stock Exchange (NSE), told reporters.
She did not say where the proposed exchange would be located but said it would be modelled on the Abidjan-based bourse of Francophone West African nations.

During the annual meeting of the African Stock Exchanges Association (ASEA) which ended in Cairo on Wednesday, Okereke-Onyuikewas was appointed to head a body to harmonise listing requirements for African stock exchanges.
She said this committee was expected to produce a basic listing requirement for the continent's exchanges next year.
Okereke-Onyuike, the assistant director general of the NSE, said the appointment of Nigeria's Hayford Alile as ASEA's new chairman was a positive development for the Nigerian market.
"He will be speaking for the whole continent for the next one year and we too will have to show a good example in our market," she said.
She said Alile's appointment was earlier resisted by some members of the 16-nation body because of Nigeria's current political problems.
"We were able to convince them that our market is immune from political considerations," Okereke-Onyuike said.
Nigeria has been in political crisis since June 1993 when the army annulled a vote meant to usher in civilian government.

Many western nations, led by the U.S., have been pressing the present rulers under threat of sanctions to restore democracy in Africa's most populous nation. The military authorities are implementing a plan to do so by October 1998.
